rounds.q: Name the highlighted bone.
rounds.why: The thumb has only two phalanges. Skier’s thumb, a torn ligament at the joint at its base, is one of the commonest hand injuries.

rounds.q: Which nerve supplies most of the small muscles inside the hand?
rounds.answer: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
wrong: Recurrent branch of the median nerve
rounds.why: It supplies the interossei, the two inner lumbricals, adductor pollicis and the little finger muscles. Damage causes clawing and a weak pinch.

rounds.q: Which muscles bend the knuckles while straightening the finger joints, making a ‘tabletop’ hand?
rounds.why: Odd little muscles: they start on the deep flexor tendons and finish on the extensor hood, linking the two systems.

rounds.q: In de Quervain’s tenosynovitis, which tendon is inflamed along with extensor pollicis brevis?
rounds.why: They share the first tunnel on the thumb side of the wrist. Common in new parents lifting babies.

rounds.q: In trigger finger, the flexor tendon catches on which pulley?
rounds.why: The A1 pulley sits over the knuckle in the palm. A steroid injection or a small release fixes most cases.

rounds.q: Which ligament is torn in most ankle sprains?
rounds.why: Rolling the foot inwards with the toes pointed stresses it first. The calcaneofibular ligament goes next in worse sprains.

rounds.q: Which bone sits on top of the heel bone and forms the lower half of the ankle joint?
rounds.why: No muscles attach to it and most of it is cartilage, so a fracture of its neck can cut off its blood supply.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted muscle.
rounds.why: It lifts the foot at the ankle. Weakness causes foot drop, often from pressure on the nerve at the top of the fibula.

rounds.q: Morton’s neuroma most often affects the nerve between which toes?
rounds.why: It’s a thickened nerve between the metatarsal heads. Tight, narrow shoes and heels make it worse.

rounds.q: Where is plantar fasciitis pain usually felt?
rounds.answer: Under the heel, towards the inner side
wrong: Back of the heel, where the Achilles attaches
rounds.why: The plantar fascia anchors on the inner front of the heel bone. Pain is classically worst with the first steps in the morning.

rounds.q: Which muscle forms most of the pelvic floor?
rounds.why: Its parts (puborectalis, pubococcygeus and iliococcygeus) form a sling that holds up the pelvic organs.

rounds.q: Which nerve carries the signal that lifts the testis in the cremasteric reflex?
rounds.why: Stroke the inner thigh and the testis rises. Its motor side runs in the genital branch (L1–L2).

rounds.q: Which muscle leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic notch, with the sciatic nerve usually just below it?
rounds.why: In some people the nerve passes through it, a variant linked, controversially, with ‘piriformis syndrome’.

rounds.q: Which two ligaments turn the sciatic notches into the greater and lesser sciatic foramina?
rounds.why: The pudendal nerve leaves through the greater foramen and hooks back in through the lesser, around the ischial spine.

rounds.q: The perineal body anchors the pelvic floor. What injures it most often?
rounds.why: It sits between the vagina and anus. Third- and fourth-degree tears reach the anal sphincter and need careful repair.

rounds.q: What’s the biggest muscle in the body?
rounds.why: It powers stairs, standing up from a chair and running uphill.

rounds.q: Which muscle gives the ‘six-pack’?
rounds.why: Tendon bands across it make the blocks. Everyone has one; body fat decides if it shows.

rounds.q: Which chest muscle do push-ups mostly work?
rounds.why: It pulls the arm across and down in front of the chest. Pec minor sits underneath.

rounds.q: Which broad back muscle powers a chin-up?
rounds.why: The ‘lats’ run from the lower back and pelvis to the front of the upper arm. Swimmers build big ones.

rounds.q: Which neck muscle stands out when you turn your head to one side?
rounds.why: It runs from behind the ear to the breastbone and collarbone. Turning left uses the right one.

rounds.q: Which muscle bulges at the angle of the jaw when you clench?
rounds.why: Pound for pound one of the strongest muscles. Teeth grinding can make it bulky and sore.

rounds.q: Which muscle closes your eyes?
rounds.why: A ring of muscle round the eye. In Bell’s palsy it weakens, so the eye needs protecting.

rounds.q: Which gland sits in front of the ear and swells in mumps?
rounds.why: The biggest salivary gland. The facial nerve runs right through it.

rounds.q: What forms the ‘Adam’s apple’?
rounds.why: Its two plates meet at a sharper angle after a testosterone-driven puberty, so it sticks out more. The vocal cords attach just behind it.

rounds.q: Which muscle raises your eyebrows and wrinkles your forehead?
rounds.why: Botox here smooths forehead lines. Too much and the brows drop.

rounds.q: Which part of the body makes cortisol?
rounds.why: The outer layer makes cortisol and aldosterone; the inner medulla makes adrenaline. The pituitary only sends the signal (ACTH).

rounds.q: Which hormone starts labour contractions and milk let-down?
rounds.why: Made in the hypothalamus, released from the back of the pituitary. Prolactin makes milk; oxytocin squeezes it out.

rounds.q: Which pancreatic cells make insulin?
rounds.why: They sit in the islets of Langerhans. Type 1 diabetes destroys them. Alpha cells make glucagon.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted organ.
rounds.why: It lies across the back of the abdomen behind the stomach, which is why pancreatic pain often goes through to the back.

rounds.q: Which hormone do the thyroid’s C cells make?
rounds.why: It slightly lowers blood calcium but does little in adults. It’s a tumour marker for medullary thyroid cancer.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted muscle.
rounds.why: A long strap on the inner thigh. Surgeons borrow it for tendon grafts and flaps.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted muscle.
rounds.why: The only quadriceps muscle that crosses the hip as well as the knee, so it’s the one strained in kicking sports.

rounds.q: Which small hip muscle lies under gluteus medius and tears along with it?
rounds.why: Both tendons attach to the greater trochanter. Tears cause outer hip pain, often labelled ‘trochanteric bursitis’.

rounds.q: Which nerve supplies the hamstrings?
rounds.why: The odd one out is the short head of biceps femoris, supplied by the common fibular division.

rounds.q: Which muscle stops your pelvis dropping on the other side when you stand on one leg?
rounds.why: If it’s weak, the pelvis sags on the lifted side: the Trendelenburg sign.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted muscle.
rounds.why: The only cuff muscle on the front of the shoulder blade. It turns the arm inwards; test it with the belly-press.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted muscle.
rounds.why: It turns the arm outwards. Test with resisted external rotation, elbow tucked at the side.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted bony hook.
rounds.why: Pec minor, short head of biceps and coracobrachialis all attach here.

rounds.q: Which nerve supplies the trapezius?
rounds.why: It runs just under the skin in the back of the neck, so a lymph node biopsy there can damage it and drop the shoulder.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted tendon.
rounds.why: It runs in a groove and into the shoulder joint. A rupture gives the ‘Popeye’ bulge in the upper arm.

rounds.q: Which tendon behind the inner ankle holds up the arch, and fails in adult flatfoot?
rounds.why: The commonest cause of flatfoot developing in adults. Ask them to rise on tiptoe on one leg.

rounds.q: Which small bones sit under the head of the first metatarsal?
rounds.why: They act like a kneecap for the big toe. Dancers and runners can fracture or inflame them.

rounds.q: A fracture at the base of the fifth metatarsal, where the shaft starts, is called a…
rounds.why: A poor blood supply there means slow healing. It often needs strict rest from weight-bearing, or surgery.

rounds.q: Which joints are injured in a Lisfranc injury?
rounds.why: Easily missed. Bruising on the sole of the midfoot is a classic clue.

rounds.q: Which nerve supplies most of the skin on the sole?
rounds.why: A branch of the tibial nerve. The lateral plantar nerve covers the rest, and the heel has its own branches.

rounds.q: The brachial plexus passes between which two muscles in the neck?
rounds.why: The subclavian artery goes with it, while the vein passes in front. It’s where an ‘interscalene’ shoulder block goes.

rounds.q: At what level does the common carotid artery usually split?
rounds.answer: Upper border of the thyroid cartilage (C3–C4)
rounds.why: The carotid sinus here senses blood pressure. Pressing on it can slow the heart.

rounds.q: Which structure is the landmark for an emergency surgical airway?
rounds.why: Feel the dip between the thyroid and cricoid cartilages. It’s thin and sits just under the skin.

rounds.q: Which nerve loop supplies the ‘strap’ muscles of the neck?
rounds.why: A loop from C1–C3 lying on the carotid sheath. Thyroid surgeons cut the straps high to spare it.

rounds.q: Infection in which space behind the throat, mainly in young children, can spread into the chest?
rounds.why: Abscesses come from infected lymph nodes there. Neck stiffness, drooling and a muffled voice are red flags.

rounds.q: Which thigh muscle makes the ‘teardrop’ just above the inner knee?
rounds.why: Its lowest fibres help keep the kneecap tracking straight.

rounds.q: ‘Groin strains’ usually involve which muscle group?
rounds.why: Adductor longus is the most commonly strained, especially in sports with quick changes of direction.

rounds.q: Which forearm muscle bulges near the elbow when you bend it with your thumb pointing up?
rounds.why: It works best in this ‘holding a cup’ position. Its reflex is tested just above the wrist.

rounds.q: Tennis elbow affects where which muscles attach?
rounds.why: Their shared tendon attaches to the outer elbow. Golfer’s elbow is the flexors on the inner side.

rounds.q: Which muscles squeeze blood in the leg veins back up to the heart when you walk?
rounds.why: The calf muscle pump. Long flights switch it off, so walk and flex your ankles.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted bone.
rounds.why: The fingertip bone. Crushing it in a door is common, and the nail bed may need repair.

rounds.q: What’s the fleshy mound at the base of the thumb called?
rounds.why: Its muscles let you bring the thumb across the palm. Wasting here suggests carpal tunnel syndrome.

rounds.q: Which nerve gives feeling to the little finger?
rounds.why: Bumping your ‘funny bone’ hits this nerve, which is why the tingle runs to the little finger.

rounds.q: How many bones are in one hand, including the wrist?
rounds.why: 8 wrist bones, 5 metacarpals and 14 phalanges. Your two hands hold over a quarter of your bones.

rounds.q: Which joint is the knuckle when you make a fist?
rounds.why: A ‘boxer’s fracture’ breaks the neck of the fifth metacarpal, just behind this knuckle.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted artery.
rounds.why: It becomes the dorsalis pedis artery, the pulse you feel on the top of the foot.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted sheet joining the two leg bones.
rounds.why: It ties the tibia and fibula together. A ‘high ankle sprain’ can tear up into it.

rounds.q: What’s the earliest warning sign of compartment syndrome?
rounds.answer: Pain out of proportion, worse with passive stretch
rounds.why: Pulses often stay present until late. Don’t wait for them; it’s a surgical emergency.

rounds.q: Which skinny calf muscle has a very long tendon, is missing in some people, and gets borrowed for grafts?
rounds.why: Its thin tendon runs between gastrocnemius and soleus.

rounds.q: Where do shin splints (medial tibial stress syndrome) hurt?
rounds.answer: Along the inner border of the tibia
wrong: Over the front of the fibula
rounds.why: Common in new runners who build up too fast. Pain at one sharp spot that hurts to hop suggests a stress fracture.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted bone.
rounds.why: Five vertebrae fused into one, wedged between the hip bones at the sacroiliac joints.

rounds.q: What’s the bony bump you sit on?
rounds.why: The hamstrings start here. Teen sprinters can pull a piece of it off before it fuses.

rounds.q: Which bony point at the front of the hip do your hands find on your hips?
rounds.why: Sartorius and the inguinal ligament start here. A skin nerve passes just inside it and can get pinched by tight belts.

rounds.q: Which joint joins the two pubic bones at the front?
rounds.why: It softens and widens slightly in pregnancy, which can cause pelvic girdle pain.

rounds.q: Which hip bone forms the top of the hip socket and the crest you rest your hands on?
rounds.why: Ilium, ischium and pubis fuse at the hip socket by the late teens. The back of the iliac crest is where bone marrow is sampled.

rounds.q: Which cheek muscle do trumpet players use?
rounds.why: It keeps the cheeks firm and pushes food back between the teeth.

rounds.q: Which muscle pulls the corners of the mouth up into a smile?
rounds.why: A genuine smile also crinkles the eyes, using orbicularis oculi.

rounds.q: Which facial nerve branch is at risk in surgery near the angle of the jaw, causing a lopsided smile?
rounds.why: It loops below the jaw line. Damage weakens the lower lip on that side.

rounds.q: With a weak side of the face, which finding points to a stroke rather than Bell’s palsy?
rounds.why: The forehead gets supply from both sides of the brain, so a stroke spares it. A facial nerve problem doesn’t.

rounds.q: Which chewing muscle opens the jaw and is often tender in jaw joint pain?
rounds.why: It attaches to the jaw joint’s disc. It’s the only chewing muscle that opens the mouth.

rounds.q: Which forearm muscle can trap the median nerve near the elbow?
rounds.why: Pronator syndrome mimics carpal tunnel, but numbness also reaches the palm.

rounds.q: Which muscle can trap the posterior interosseous nerve, causing finger drop without wrist drop?
rounds.why: The nerve passes through it under a fibrous arch. Wrist extension is spared because those muscles are supplied higher up.

rounds.q: Which thumb tendon can snap weeks after a wrist fracture, even an undisplaced one?
rounds.why: It hooks round a bony bump on the back of the radius and can fray there. The thumb tip then can’t lift.

rounds.q: Which muscle bends the fingertip joint?
rounds.why: Hold the middle finger joint still and ask for a tip bend. ‘Jersey finger’ is when its tendon tears off.

rounds.q: Which nerve branch is damaged if someone can’t make an ‘OK’ sign but has no numbness?
wrong: Recurrent branch of the median nerve
rounds.why: A purely motor branch of the median nerve. With no numbness, it’s often mistaken for a tendon rupture.

rounds.q: Which tendon runs in a groove under a ledge of the heel bone, and troubles ballet dancers?
rounds.why: ‘Dancer’s tendinitis’ hurts behind the inner ankle when rising onto the toes.

rounds.q: Which ligament, the ‘spring’ ligament, cradles the head of the talus?
rounds.why: It holds up the inner arch and often fails along with the tibialis posterior tendon.

rounds.q: Which inner midfoot bone is where tibialis posterior mainly attaches, and sometimes has an extra bone?
rounds.why: An accessory navicular is a common painful bump on the inner midfoot.

rounds.q: Which nerve is trapped in ‘Baxter’s nerve’ heel pain?
rounds.answer: First branch of the lateral plantar nerve
rounds.why: An easily missed cause of stubborn heel pain, often blamed on plantar fasciitis.

rounds.q: Which small bone behind the talus causes back-of-ankle pain in ballet dancers and fast bowlers?
rounds.why: An unfused piece of the talus. Pointing the foot pinches it.

rounds.q: Which deep abdominal muscle wraps round the waist like a corset?
rounds.why: It tightens the abdomen and helps brace the spine before you lift.

rounds.q: Which long muscles run either side of the spine and straighten your back?
rounds.why: Most ‘back strains’ involve them.

rounds.q: Which diamond-shaped muscle spans your upper back and shrugs your shoulders?
rounds.why: The upper part is where many people carry neck and shoulder tension.

rounds.q: Which muscles between the ribs help you breathe?
rounds.why: Nerves and vessels run under each rib, so chest drains go in just above a rib.

rounds.q: Which deep muscle between the lowest rib and the pelvis is often tight in low back pain?
rounds.why: It hitches the hip and steadies the spine when you stand on one leg.

rounds.q: Which hormone does the pancreas release when blood sugar is high?
rounds.why: It moves glucose into cells. Glucagon does the opposite when sugar is low.

rounds.q: Which hormone rises at night to make you sleepy?
rounds.why: Bright screens at night suppress it. Morning light helps reset the body clock.

rounds.q: Which ovarian hormone builds up the lining of the uterus in the first half of the cycle?
rounds.why: After ovulation, progesterone takes over and readies the lining for a pregnancy.

rounds.q: Which hormone do the testes mainly make?
rounds.why: It drives puberty changes, muscle and sperm production.

rounds.q: Which ‘hunger hormone’ rises before meals?
rounds.why: Made mainly in the stomach. Leptin, from fat tissue, signals fullness over the long term.

rounds.q: Which ring of cartilage is the only complete ring in the airway?
rounds.why: It sits at C6. It was long taught as the narrowest part of a child’s airway.

rounds.q: Which thin muscle just under the skin of the neck tightens when you grimace?
rounds.why: A face muscle that has slipped into the neck. The neck ‘bands’ that come with age are its edges.

rounds.q: Which two-bellied strap muscle runs from the shoulder blade to the hyoid bone?
rounds.why: Its middle tendon lies over the internal jugular vein, a handy surgical landmark.

rounds.q: Damage to what in the neck causes a droopy eyelid, small pupil and less sweating on one side of the face?
rounds.why: That’s Horner syndrome. Neck causes include carotid dissection and tumours at the top of the lung.

rounds.q: Which neck vein can you see swell when you strain?
rounds.why: It crosses sternocleidomastoid. Venous pressure (JVP) is judged from the deeper internal jugular.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted bone.
rounds.why: The stiffest metacarpal, locked onto the wrist, giving the index finger a solid base for pinch.

rounds.q: Which muscles spread the fingers apart?
rounds.why: Memory aid: DAB (dorsal abduct) and PAD (palmar adduct). All are supplied by the ulnar nerve.

rounds.q: Which thumb muscle wastes in severe carpal tunnel syndrome?
rounds.why: Test by lifting the thumb straight up off the palm against resistance.

rounds.q: A finger held slightly bent, swollen and agony to straighten after a puncture suggests infection where?
rounds.why: These are Kanavel’s signs. It’s a hand surgery emergency.

rounds.q: Which muscle pulls the thumb against the side of the hand, as in holding a key?
rounds.why: If it’s weak, the thumb tip bends to grip paper: Froment’s sign.

rounds.q: Which part of levator ani forms a sling behind the rectum?
rounds.why: It kinks the rectum to help keep you continent. If it won’t relax, it causes one type of constipation.

rounds.q: Which anal sphincter can you squeeze on purpose?
rounds.why: It’s skeletal muscle. The internal sphincter is smooth muscle and keeps resting tone automatically.

rounds.q: Which spinal nerve roots mainly supply the pelvic floor and sphincters?
rounds.why: That’s why cauda equina compression causes saddle numbness and bladder or bowel trouble. It’s an emergency.

rounds.q: Which reflex checks the pelvic floor’s nerve supply by stroking near the anus?
rounds.why: A quick squeeze of the external sphincter. If it’s missing, think S2–S4 or cauda equina.

rounds.q: Which ligament at the base of the broad ligament runs sideways from the cervix and carries the uterine artery?
rounds.why: The ureter passes just under the uterine artery here: ‘water under the bridge’, a known trap in hysterectomy.

rounds.q: Which deep back muscle, in short bundles over a few vertebrae, often shrinks after low back pain?
rounds.why: Scans often show it smaller and fattier in people with long-term back pain.

rounds.q: Which muscles pull the shoulder blades together?
rounds.why: They join the inner border of the shoulder blade to the spine.

rounds.q: Which muscle runs from the upper neck to the top corner of the shoulder blade and is sore in stiff necks?
rounds.why: Its lower end is a classic tender spot in desk workers.

rounds.q: Which muscle pulls the shoulder blade forward round the chest, as in a punch?
rounds.why: If its nerve is damaged, the shoulder blade ‘wings’ when pushing against a wall.

rounds.q: Which small muscles at the top of the neck tilt the head and feature in tension headaches?
rounds.why: Four small muscles between the skull and the top two vertebrae, close to the greater occipital nerve.

rounds.q: What passes through Guyon’s canal at the wrist?
wrong: Ulnar nerve and flexor carpi ulnaris tendon
Radial artery and superficial radial nerve
rounds.why: The canal lies between the pisiform and the hook of the hamate. Long-distance cyclists can squash the nerve here.

rounds.q: Which structure tears in a boutonnière deformity?
rounds.answer: Central slip of the extensor tendon
rounds.why: The middle joint pokes through like a button through a buttonhole. Early splinting prevents it becoming fixed.

rounds.q: A mallet finger is a tear of which structure?
rounds.why: The fingertip droops and can’t straighten. Six weeks or more of continuous splinting usually works.

rounds.q: Which lumbricals are supplied by the median nerve?
rounds.why: The ulnar nerve supplies the third and fourth, which is why ulnar palsy claws mainly the ring and little fingers.

rounds.q: Which ligament is torn in skier’s (gamekeeper’s) thumb?
rounds.answer: Ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb MCP joint
wrong: Radial collateral ligament of the thumb MCP joint
Volar plate of the thumb IP joint
rounds.why: If the torn end flips behind a tendon sheet (a Stener lesion), it won’t heal without surgery.

rounds.q: Which hamstring tears most often in sprinting?
rounds.why: Usually the long head, as the leg reaches forward at top speed.

rounds.q: A ‘corked thigh’ is a bruise of which muscle group?
rounds.why: Gentle movement and no early massage lower the risk of bone forming in the muscle.

rounds.q: Which muscle tears in ‘tennis leg’?
rounds.why: Sudden sharp pain in the inner calf, like being hit with a stone, typically in middle age.

rounds.q: Pec tears in weightlifters usually happen during which exercise?
rounds.why: The tendon tears near the arm as the bar comes down. Surgery is usually advised in active people.

rounds.q: Which tendon is affected in ‘jumper’s knee’?
rounds.why: Pain at the lower tip of the kneecap. Loading exercises are the main treatment.

rounds.q: How many bones are in each foot?
rounds.why: 7 tarsals, 5 metatarsals and 14 phalanges. Your hands and feet hold over half your bones.

rounds.q: Which bone forms the bump on the inside of the ankle?
rounds.why: The outer bump is the fibula, and it sits lower.

rounds.q: What’s the arch along the inner side of the foot called?
rounds.why: Most flexible flat feet in children are normal and need no treatment.

rounds.q: What’s the thick band under the sole that supports the arch?
rounds.why: It works like a bowstring for the arch.

rounds.q: Gout most often first strikes which joint?
rounds.why: Crystals form more easily in cooler joints. A hot, red, exquisitely tender joint overnight is typical.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted muscle.
rounds.why: The broadest hamstring. Its tendon helps support the back of the knee joint.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted vein.
rounds.why: The longest vein in the body. The commonest site of varicose veins and a favourite bypass graft.

rounds.q: Which three tendons form the pes anserinus on the inner knee?
rounds.why: Memory aid: ‘Say Grace before Tea’. Bursitis here hurts just below the inner joint line.

rounds.q: Which small muscle behind the knee unlocks the straight knee?
rounds.why: It twists the knee slightly to unlock it. Its tendon runs inside the joint near the lateral meniscus.

rounds.q: The iliotibial band attaches to which bump on the outer tibia?
rounds.why: ITB friction pain is usually felt higher, over the outer femur just above the joint.

rounds.q: Which fan-shaped chewing muscle sits at the temple?
rounds.why: Feel it tighten when you clench. New temple pain over 50 also raises giant cell arteritis.

rounds.q: In jaw joint (TMJ) disorder, what usually causes the clicking?
rounds.why: The disc slips forward and pops back as the mouth opens. Most cases settle with jaw rest and less clenching.

rounds.q: Which muscle purses your lips to whistle?
rounds.why: A ring of muscle round the mouth, supplied by the facial nerve.

rounds.q: Which salivary gland most often forms stones?
rounds.why: Its saliva is thicker and its duct runs uphill. Swelling under the jaw at mealtimes is the clue.

rounds.q: Which muscle wrinkles your chin when you sulk?
rounds.why: It pushes up the lower lip. An overactive one gives a dimpled ‘orange peel’ chin.

rounds.q: Which layer of the adrenal cortex makes aldosterone?
rounds.why: From outside in: salt, sugar, sex (aldosterone, cortisol, androgens).

rounds.q: Excess of which pituitary hormone causes acromegaly?
rounds.why: Growth plates have closed in adults, so hands, feet, jaw and soft tissues enlarge. IGF-1 is the screening test.

rounds.q: Which structure connects the hypothalamus to the pituitary?
rounds.why: Pressure on it can raise prolactin, because the brake signal (dopamine) can’t get through.

rounds.q: A pituitary tumour pressing upwards classically causes which visual field loss?
rounds.why: It presses on the optic chiasm, where fibres serving the outer visual fields cross.

rounds.q: Which thyroid hormone is the more active form inside cells?
rounds.why: The thyroid mainly releases T4, which tissues convert to T3. That’s why T4 replacement alone works for most people.

rounds.q: Which short hip rotator leaves the pelvis through the lesser sciatic foramen?
rounds.why: It wraps sharply around the ischium, using it like a pulley.

rounds.q: Which muscle runs from the front of the pelvis into the iliotibial band?
rounds.why: It tightens the ITB. Runners and cyclists can overload it.

rounds.q: Name the highlighted muscle.
rounds.why: The tendon you feel in the groin. It forms the inner edge of the femoral triangle.

rounds.q: Which ligament, among the strongest in the body, reinforces the front of the hip?
rounds.why: Its Y shape stops the hip over-extending, so you can stand with little muscle effort.

rounds.q: Which artery mainly supplies the femoral head in adults?
rounds.why: Displaced hip fractures inside the joint tear its branches, which is why they’re often replaced rather than fixed.

rounds.q: Which muscle belly on top of the foot helps tell a deep fibular nerve or L5 problem?
rounds.why: It’s the only muscle mass on the top of the foot. Wasting suggests a nerve problem.

rounds.q: Which muscle lifts the upper eyelid?
rounds.why: An oculomotor palsy drops the lid fully. Horner syndrome causes only a mild droop, through Müller’s muscle.

rounds.q: Which middle ear muscle damps loud sounds, alongside stapedius?
rounds.why: It tenses the eardrum via the malleus. It’s supplied by V3, while stapedius gets the facial nerve.

rounds.q: Which muscle forms the floor of the mouth?
rounds.why: Infection from lower molars spreading below it can cause Ludwig’s angina, which threatens the airway.

rounds.q: Which muscle forms the outer floor of the femoral triangle?
rounds.why: Inside the triangle lie the femoral nerve, artery and vein: NAV, from outside in.
